items.stem: What is the core idea behind contrastive image-text training such as CLIP?

options.text: Learn a shared space where matching image and text pairs are close together
options.rationale: Correct: contrastive training aligns image and text embeddings for matching pairs.

options.text: Convert every image into English sentences before training
options.rationale: It aligns embeddings; it does not pre-translate images to text.

options.text: Train the vision and language parts to never interact
options.rationale: The point is to relate the two modalities, not isolate them.

options.text: Remove all text from the training data
options.rationale: Text is essential to the image-text pairing.

items.explanation: Correct: contrastive training aligns image and text embeddings for matching pairs.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate tasks for a vision-language model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Answering questions about the contents of an image
options.rationale: Correct: visual question answering is a core VLM task.

options.text: Generating a caption describing an image
options.rationale: Correct: captioning is a standard VLM task.

options.text: Sorting a numeric database with no images or text
options.rationale: That is a plain data task, not multimodal.
Code compilation is unrelated to vision-language models.

items.explanation: Correct: visual question answering is a core VLM task.

items.stem: A vision-language model confidently reports an object that is not actually in the image. What is this failure called?

options.rationale: Correct: the model fabricates content not supported by the input.
That stems from low-precision numerics, not fabricated content.
Overfitting is a training issue, not a per-image fabrication.
Latency is a speed measure, not an incorrect-content issue.

items.explanation: Correct: the model fabricates content not supported by the input.
